survey: A cartoon refracting telescope on a small stand, on a grey lunar-style surface. The cream tube points up and to the right. The wide end, with the blue objective lens and an orange-gold cap, faces the camera at the top right. The narrow eyepiece, a gold ring with a dark grey cup, sits at the lower left. The tube rests in a grey cradle (a yoke). A round pivot bolt on the side of the cradle lets the tube tilt up and down. The cradle is bolted onto a grey square plate, which sits on a round orange wooden hub with a gold ring under it. Wooden legs splay out from under the hub and end in grey rubber feet, all of which touch the ground and cast shadows. The optics are in the right order: lens at the front, eyepiece at the back. The mount is plausible.

errors.where: Stand legs, especially the left side of the stand
errors.what: The stand has four legs where a telescope tripod has three: one at the left back, one at the front left, one in the middle back and one at the right. The two left legs leave the hub almost side by side and run nearly parallel to separate feet, so they look like one leg drawn twice. The leg layout around the hub is also uneven.

fix: Telescope on a classic three-legged wooden tripod: exactly three legs, spaced evenly around the round hub at 120 degrees and splayed outward, each ending in one grey rubber foot on the ground. No fourth leg, no doubled legs.
